inputs.notes: OWNER FCF BASIS: FY2025 reported FCF $360.4M less SBC-incl-equity-award-taxes $148.6M less interest income $45.2M = $166.6M. Interest income is stripped because net cash is added to enterprise value at the end of the DCF — counting the interest it earns inside FCF as well would value the $1.14B cash pile twice. Forward SBC is projected as a declining % of revenue (15.0% -> 12.5% base), not as a flat dollar amount. DUOL has repurchased no shares, so the full SBC is uncovered dilution and shares grow 2.15%/yr to 54.51M by year 5.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, 'Stock-based compensation expenses related to equity awards' = $148,643K. This is the company's own combined figure; it is NOT the $137.4M cash-flow add-back plus the $41.6M of net-share-settlement taxes (that sum, $179.0M, would double-count).

historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Historical CAGRs (revenue 3yr: 41.1%, FCF 3yr: 70.4%, equity 2yr: 51.8%) reflect the 2022-2025 hypergrowth phase and are not representative of the current trajectory. FY2026 guidance of +15-18% revenue growth (midpoint ~17%) anchors Year 1 because it reflects the deliberate strategic pivot to user growth over monetization and the bookings deceleration underway. EPS CAGRs are excluded as unreliable due to inconsistent profitability history and the large one-time deferred tax valuation-allowance release in Q3 2025 ($256.7M), which inflated FY2025 GAAP net income to $414.1M. Normalized FY2025 net income is approximately $157.4M.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical growth rates are structurally elevated and not suitable as DCF base. Revenue 3yr CAGR (41.1%) and FCF 3yr CAGR (70.4%) far exceed sustainable long-run growth. FY2026 guidance represents a significant deceleration: bookings growth slowing from 33% to 10-12%, Adj. EBITDA margins compressing ~370bps to ~25.7%. Selected growth rate anchored to guidance, not historical CAGRs.

notes.eps_excluded: EPS CAGR unreliable: FY2025 GAAP EPS of $8.38 is inflated by a $256.7M one-time deferred tax valuation-allowance release (Q3 2025). Normalized FY2025 EPS is approximately $3.21 ($157.4M / 49.0M shares). GAAP net income should not be used as a DCF base.
notes.equity_cagr_limited: Only 2-year equity CAGR available (FY2023-FY2025) as earlier balance sheet data not in dataset. Equity CAGR of 51.8% reflects early-stage profitability buildup and is not suitable as a steady-state growth proxy.
notes.fcf_margin_note: FCF margin (34.7% of revenue in FY2025) is structurally higher than Adj EBITDA margin (29.5%) due to: (1) deferred revenue from annual subscriptions creating favorable working capital; (2) very low capex (~$27.4M in FY2025, 2.6% of revenue); (3) continued tax benefit utilization. FY2026 FCF guided >$350M (roughly flat vs FY2025) despite EBITDA margin compression, demonstrating FCF resilience.
notes.q3_2025_normalization: Q3 2025 net income of $292.2M includes approximately $256.7M in non-recurring deferred tax valuation-allowance release. This is a one-time accounting item with no cash impact and is excluded from all FCF-based projections, which are the correct basis for DUOL's valuation given the FCF >> GAAP net income dynamic from SBC and deferred revenue.
notes.sbc_adjusted_fcf: FCF CAGRs above are on REPORTED FCF. On the SBC-adjusted series the 3yr CAGR is not meaningful (FY2022 adjusted FCF was negative, -$0.5M), and the 2yr adjusted CAGR of 117.8% exceeds the reported 59.2% only because the FY2023 base is depressed by SBC — a low-base artifact, not accelerating growth. Neither figure drives the projections; scenario growth is anchored to FY2026 revenue guidance.

base.name: Base Case: Guided Deceleration Then Recovery
base.description: FY2026 is a deliberate investment year. Revenue growth follows guidance (17%) before re-accelerating in FY2027-2028 as the expanded user base (targeting 100M DAUs from 52.7M in FY2025) drives higher monetization. Growth then moderates as the company scales toward $2B+ revenue. FCF margin maintained at 33% reflecting structural FCF conversion advantage even as EBITDA margin is guided to compress to ~25.7%.
base.reasoning: Y1 (17%): Per FY2026 guidance midpoint (+15-18%). Y2-Y3 (20-22%): Re-acceleration as user growth investments pay off, DAU growth recovers from ~21% toward 100M DAU target, and Max tier adoption expands. Y4-Y5 (18-15%): Natural deceleration as company approaches $1.8B-$2B revenue scale. FCF margin of 33% reflects structural FCF conversion advantage (deferred revenue, low capex, tax shield utilization) consistent with FY2025 actual FCF margin of 34.7%.

bull.name: Bull Case: AI Platform Shift Succeeds, DAU Target Achieved
bull.description: The AI-first strategy proves as transformative as the 2013 mobile bet. Duolingo reaches 100M DAUs by 2028, driving strong bookings re-acceleration. Max tier adoption accelerates as AI features (Video Call, Roleplay, personalized content) differentiate against free AI tools. Adjacent subjects (Chess, Math, Music) begin contributing meaningfully to revenue.
bull.reasoning: Y1 (20%): Slight beat to guidance as early investment pays off faster than expected. Y2-Y3 (28-25%): Significant re-acceleration as 100M DAU milestone drives monetization leverage; Chess, Math, Music contribute. Y4-Y5 (22-18%): Strong but moderating growth. FCF margin of 36% reflects operating leverage as revenue scales past $2B on a relatively fixed-cost tech platform. Lower WACC (9%) justified by stronger execution track record and reduced risk. Terminal growth of 4% supported by projected 18% CAGR in online language learning market through 2035.

bear.name: Bear Case: Investment Cycle Fails, Competitive Erosion
bear.description: The FY2026 investment year fails to reignite user growth. Bookings deceleration proves structural rather than strategic. AI competitors (ChatGPT, Gemini) erode Duolingo's unique value proposition faster than the company can respond. The 2026 EBITDA compression becomes a permanent margin reset. Top-of-funnel stays flat and Video Call migration from Max to Super tier compresses ARPU.
bear.reasoning: Y1 (15%): At low-end of guidance range; bookings stay depressed. Y2 (12%): Investment year shows limited DAU re-acceleration. Y3-Y5 (10-6%): Structural growth deceleration as market saturation, AI competition, and effectiveness concerns limit expansion. FCF margin of 28% reflects permanent margin compression as AI cost inflation structurally shifts the gross margin from 73% toward 69% with limited recovery path. Higher WACC (11.5%) reflects elevated execution risk, CFO transition uncertainty, and competitive deterioration. Terminal growth of 2% reflects mature, slower-growing business.

sanity_check.assessment: Base IV $87.97 sits 37.5% BELOW the current price of $140.73; probability-weighted $91.84 is 34.7% below. Only the bull case (+6.4%) clears today's price. The valuation is demanding once FY2025's deferred-revenue windfall (34% of reported FCF) and tax benefit are normalized away. No trip conditions fired: owner FCF rises every year, WACC 10% suits a debt-free platform, terminal growth 3% is at long-run GDP, and terminal margins are matured (16.4%) rather than mid-ramp.
sanity_check.sbc_sensitivity: SBC is the dominant swing factor. Base case assumes SBC falls from 15.0% to 12.5% of revenue over five years. If it merely holds at 15%, IV falls further; if DUOL starts repurchasing at scale, the 2.15%/yr dilution abates but the expense — and the cash cost — remain.
sanity_check.margin_normalization: The single largest driver. Carrying FY2025s 16.1% owner-FCF margin forward would give ~$113; the component build starts at 11.2% because the deferred-revenue tailwind shrinks with growth and the tax benefit expires.

valuation_philosophy.rationale:
Built on OWNER FREE CASH FLOW with margins constructed from components each year, over a 10-year horizon.
FY2025 owner FCF = $360.4M reported − $148.6M SBC (company's adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation figure) − $45.2M interest income = $166.6M.
Crucially, that FY2025 margin is NOT carried forward. Each projected year is built as: adjusted EBITDA, less SBC (a declining % of revenue), less D&A, taxed at a ramping cash rate, plus D&A, less capex, plus working capital captured on the CHANGE in revenue. Three things this exposes that a flat margin hides:
(1) DEFERRED REVENUE IS A GROWTH TAILWIND, NOT A MARGIN. The FY2025 deferred-revenue increase was $123.3M — 34% of the entire $360.4M reported FCF. It scales with bookings growth, so it shrinks hard as growth decelerates from 33% to ~10%. Stripping it, the underlying FY2025 owner-FCF margin was 4.2%, not 16.1%. Modelling it as 18% of the YoY revenue increase gives a year-1 owner-FCF margin of 11.2%, not the 15.4% a flat-margin model would carry forward.
(2) THE FY2025 TAX RATE IS NOT REPEATABLE. DUOL had a $256.7M valuation-allowance release and guides a −6% cash tax BENEFIT for 2026. The model ramps this to 21% by 2030; assuming the benefit persists is a large silent overstatement.
(3) A 5-YEAR HORIZON WOULD UNDERVALUE THE BUSINESS. Owner-FCF margin is still climbing at year 5 (13.2%) and only matures near 16.4% by year 10. Capitalizing the year-5 margin in perpetuity gives $76.21; running to year 10 where the margin has flattened gives $87.97. Capitalize a matured margin, not a ramping one.
SBC is charged exactly once: as an expense, plus only the dilution buybacks fail to absorb. DUOL has repurchased nothing (the $400M program is authorized but unspent), so shares grow 2.15%/yr to 60.6M by year 10.
valuation_philosophy.premium_multiple_justification: High-growth consumer tech platforms with dominant moats, recurring subscription revenue, and 30%+ FCF margins historically command premium multiples (20-50x FCF at maturity) because: (1) FCF compounds at high rates over long duration; (2) subscription revenue has high visibility and retention; (3) dominant market position creates a durable competitive advantage. Forcing DUOL to a market-average 15-20x FCF would be analytically inappropriate given these characteristics. Our WACC range of 9-11.5% implicitly prices the risk premium without artificially capping the multiple.
key_risks_to_framework: If AI competition materially erodes Duolingo's pricing power or user retention, the FCF margin and growth assumptions would need to be revised downward — the bear case models this at 28% FCF margin and 6% terminal growth
If interest rates rise materially above current levels, WACC would need upward revision — the sensitivity matrix covers up to 12% WACC
If the FY2026 investment year fails to re-accelerate DAUs, the base case growth recovery (20-22% in Y2-Y3) may need to be revised toward the bear case trajectory

sbc_treatment.policy: Owner FCF: less SBC (incl. equity-award taxes), less interest income; forward SBC as declining % of revenue; shares diluted only by what buybacks do not absorb
sbc_treatment.progression_of_estimates: Unadjusted (SBC added back, 5yr): $204.79. Less flat SBC: $134.74. Full owner FCF, flat margin: $113.27. Component-built margin, 5yr: $76.21 (capitalizes a still-ramping 13.2% margin). Component-built margin, 10yr: $87.97 <- current. An independent 10yr model (DCFs/DUOL_FCF_Model_Jul2026.xlsx, built by Claude Fable 5) lands at $100.61; the residual difference is share dilution — that model holds shares flat at 49.8M on the reasoning that expensing SBC removes the need to dilute, whereas this model also grows the count by the ~2.15%/yr of dilution DUOL's zero buybacks fail to absorb.
sbc_treatment.history_note: Owner FCF history: FY2022 $73.3M reported -> -$0.5M; FY2023 $142.2M -> $35.5M; FY2024 $218.0M -> $55.0M; FY2025 $360.4M -> $166.6M. In FY2022 the entire reported FCF was paid in stock.
sbc_treatment.memo_if_sbc_non_cash: If SBC were treated as non-cash (company-style), base IV would be far higher. The spread between the two is the honest measure of how much this valuation depends on SBC treatment.

margin_construction.note: Working capital modelled as 18% of the YoY revenue increase, not as a share of revenue.

key_assumptions_summary.why_guidance_based_growth: Duolingo's 2022-2025 hypergrowth (revenue CAGR 41%, FCF CAGR 70%) was exceptional and is explicitly not the basis for this DCF. The company has communicated clearly that FY2026 is a deliberate deceleration year with bookings guidance of only +10.5% (vs. +33% in FY2025). Using historical CAGRs as a base would produce dramatically overvalued results disconnected from current reality. Anchoring to the 17% FY2026 guidance midpoint and modeling a recovery arc is the most analytically sound approach.
key_assumptions_summary.fcf_vs_ebitda_margin: FCF margin (33% base case) differs from Adj. EBITDA margin (~25.7% FY2026 guidance) due to: (1) deferred revenue from annual subscriptions creates favorable working capital ($50-80M annual benefit); (2) very low capex ($27.4M in FY2025, ~2.6% of revenue, growing modestly); (3) continued tax benefits from deferred tax asset utilization. Consistent with FY2025 actual (FCF $360.4M = 34.7% margin vs. Adj. EBITDA margin of 29.5%).
key_assumptions_summary.net_cash_position: Net cash position of $1,138.6M (Q1 2026, zero debt) adds significant value above enterprise value. This represents approximately $23.24 per share in cash (vs. $20.81 at prior valuation). The $400M buyback program (no expiration) is authorized alongside growth investments, providing capital return optionality.
key_assumptions_summary.terminal_growth_justification: 3% terminal growth (base) is consistent with long-run nominal GDP growth. Online language learning market is projected to grow at 18% CAGR through 2035 per Business Research Insights, providing structural tailwinds. The bear case uses 2%, the bull case uses 4% given stronger market position assumptions.
key_assumptions_summary.wacc_justification: 10% WACC (base) reflects: risk-free rate ~4.3%, equity risk premium ~5%, beta ~1.05 (high-growth consumer tech with strong recurring revenue). Zero debt means WACC equals cost of equity with no leverage adjustment. Bear case uses 11.5% for elevated execution risk; bull case uses 9% for reduced risk at higher conviction.
key_assumptions_summary.eps_normalization: FY2025 GAAP net income of $414.1M includes a $256.7M one-time non-cash deferred tax valuation-allowance release recognized in Q3 2025. Normalized FY2025 net income is approximately $157.4M (normalized EPS ~$3.21). This normalization is critical to avoid using a distorted earnings base. FCF is not affected by this accounting item.

investment_recommendation.summary: On SBC-adjusted FCF, DUOL is roughly fairly valued to modestly expensive at $140.73. Base case IV $134.74 implies -4.3% downside; probability-weighted IV $139.57 is within 1% of the current price. This is a material reversal from the prior unadjusted model, which showed 86% upside — the difference is entirely the $137.4M of annual SBC now charged as an expense plus ~2%/yr dilution. The bull case ($205.37) still offers 46% upside if the AI platform bet and 100M DAU target land, and the balance sheet ($1.14B net cash, zero debt) bounds the downside, but the margin of safety a value investor requires is not present at this price.
investment_recommendation.bull_thesis: FY2026 investment cycle mirrors the successful 2022-2023 playbook that drove DAUs from 20M to 50M+ and built a durable monetization engine. AI content velocity (20,500 course units/quarter in Q1 2026 vs. 1,800/quarter in 2024) is widening the product moat against every competitor. If the strategy works, Duolingo could reach 80-100M DAUs by 2028, driving a re-acceleration in bookings and margins. The 78% decline from peak has created a historically rare entry point into a dominant consumer platform.
key_risks: Bookings deceleration may be structural rather than strategic: Q2 2026 bookings guided to just +6% YoY; if DAU growth does not re-accelerate materially in H2 2026, the investment thesis breaks
AI competitors (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) improving as language tutors represents a secular competitive threat that could permanently cap user growth and ARPU
Gross margin structural compression from 73% to ~69% by Q4 2026 driven by AI feature costs; this may be a permanent reset, not a temporary headwind
CFO transition risk: Gillian Munson joined February 23, 2026 — her first full year of guidance-setting is during a deliberate strategy reset
Max tier ARPU cannibalization: Video Call feature reportedly migrating from $14/month Max to the broader $7/month Super tier, compressing revenue per subscriber
key_catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings (expected August 2026): Evidence of DAU re-acceleration or bookings recovery from the Q2 trough would be the primary catalyst
H2 2026 bookings recovery: Management guided H2 to be materially stronger than H1; any early signs of bookings improvement would re-rate the stock
Duolingo Max tier penetration data: Evidence that premium AI features are converting at scale (currently ~9% of paid base) would validate the platform bet
Share buyback execution: $400M program represents ~6.7% of current market cap; aggressive buyback at current prices would be highly accretive
DAU re-acceleration evidence: Top-of-funnel described as 'about flat' in Q1 2026; any improvement in new user registration data would shift sentiment
investment_recommendation.margin_of_safety: At $140.73, the stock trades 4% ABOVE base case IV ($134.74) on SBC-adjusted FCF. Net cash of $23.24/share (17% of the price) is a hard floor, and the bear case ($83.43) implies 41% downside. Entry at the 15% IRR hurdle requires $113.92 — about 19% below today. 14 of 25 sensitivity cells now sit below the current price, versus zero before the SBC adjustment.
